newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 1998 GDP growth seen at 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 1998 GDP growth seen at 8.5 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's economy is expected to grow at 8.2 percent in 1997 and 8.5 percent in 1998, against 8.2 percent last year, government-backed think tank Malaysian Institutte of Economic Research said on Tuesday.

"MIER's forecast of real GDP growth for 1997 remains unchanged at 8.2 percent barring any sustained increase in interest rates. Growth will pick up to 8.5 percent in 1998 in tandem with better export performance and higher growth in private expenditure," MIER said in its second quarter 1997 update on the economy.
MIER said private consumption in the economy was expected to remain robust, growing by 7.1 percent in 1997 and 8.1 percent in 1998.
It said that Malaysia's exports will increase in the current year and in 1998 due to an improvement in global demand for semi-conductors.
"Overall, the current account balance is projected to see its deficit trimmed slightly to 12.5 billion ringgit in 1997 but rising to 13.3 billion ringgit in 1998," MIER said.
It said that Malaysia's merchandise exports in 1997 will grow by 6.3 percent and will improve to 11.6 percent in 1998.
Merchandise imports are forecast to rise by 6.0 percent in 1997 and 11.5 percent in 1998, MIER said.
"Inflation is forecast to be at 3.0 percent in 1997 and 3.2 percent in 1998," it said.
"Following a dampened growth last year, private investment will recover in 1997, sustained by domestic activities and emerging sign of recovery in export sector.
"It is forecast to grow by 12 percent in 1997 and 13.6 percent in 1998," it said.
MIER said its business conditions survey in the second quarter of 1997 showed that overall manufacturing sales grew at a brisk pace.
"Manufacturers were positive about the near-term export sale with the majority projecting an improvement in the next quarter," it said.
